Issued at 300 AM EDT Tue Jul 21 2026

Today-Tonight...Tropical Storm Bertha remains across the 
northeastern Gulf and is forecast to linger, slowly moving west- 
northwest today. While there will continue to be no direct impacts
across east central Florida, this particular set-up will keep 
south to southeast winds in place locally. The tight pressure 
gradient due to the proximity of Bertha will also keep conditions 
breezy and gusty at times, with wind speeds of 10 to 15 mph and 
wind gusts up to 20 mph possible. Wind enhancements due to the 
development of the east coast sea breeze will also be possible at
times. While drier air is lifting northward across the Florida 
peninsula as seen on the GOES 19 Total PWAT viewer and will help 
limit rain and storm chances today, there continues to be hi-res 
guidance supporting isolated to scattered development this 
afternoon, primarily due to sea breeze interactions across the 
central Florida peninsula. Have kept a 20-30% chance of showers 
and storms across the interior this afternoon, with isolated 
northward-moving showers and storms possible across the local 
Atlantic waters. Steep low-level lapse rates, SBCAPE of 1500-2000 
J/kg, and drier air aloft pushing DCAPE values to 1000+ J/kg will 
support frequent lightning strikes and wind gusts to 50 mph with 
any storms that manage to develop. Heavy downpours and minor,
localized flooding also cannot be ruled out. Activity across the 
peninsula is forecast to diminish into the evening hours, with 
lingering showers and storms possible across the local waters.

Above normal temperatures in the mid 90s are forecast areawide 
this afternoon, combining with humid conditions to create peak 
heat indices of 100-107F. Adequate hydration, frequent breaks in 
the shade or an air-conditioned building, and lightweight, lightly
colored clothing will all be crucial for those spending extended 
periods of time outdoors to reduce the risk of developing heat- 
related illness. Lows remain in the 70s.

Wednesday-Thursday...Tropical Storm Bertha will continue westward
across the northern Gulf through the middle of this week, which 
will allow the Atlantic high to lift northwestward towards the 
Florida peninsula. The pressure gradient will gradually weaken 
across east central Florida, especially by Thursday. South to 
southeast winds will remain between 10 to 15 mph on Wednesday with
gusts to 20 mph possible at times. By Thursday, wind speeds fall 
to 5 to 10 mph. Wind speed enhancements due to the sea breeze will
be possible, particularly along the coast. A dry air mass in the 
wake of Bertha is anticipated to remain in place locally, helping 
to limit rain and storm chances to around 20% or less across east 
central Florida both Wednesday and Thursday. Any showers or storms
that do manage to develop will likely be along or ahead of the 
sea breezes, with activity diminishing into the evening hours. 
Overall, anticipate mostly dry conditions across east central 
Florida through Thursday. The drier air will also help limit 
cloud coverage, and with the return of high pressure overhead, 
temperatures are forecast to trend warmer locally. Highs in the 
low to mid 90s are anticipated, with the warmest temperatures 
focused near and north of the I-4 corridor. Peak heat indices of 
100-107F are forecast each afternoon, so those spending extended 
periods of time outdoors will need to remain adequately hydrated 
and take frequent breaks in the shade or an air-conditioned 
building to avoid heat-related illness. Overnight, near-nromal 
temperatures are forecast with lows in the 70s.

Friday-Monday...Broad mid-level ridging will remain in place 
across the southern US late this week, with a trough across the 
eastern US gradually digging southward towards Florida into this 
weekend and early next week. At the surface, broad high pressure 
is forecast to remain situated across the local Atlantic waters on
Friday, with the high gradually pushing southward this weekend as
a low moves offshore the Carolinas and drags a frontal boundary 
southward across the southeastern US. The boundary will stall 
across north Florida on Sunday, continuing to drift southward 
towards the peninsula into early next week as it weakens. Locally,
lingering dry air across the area on Friday will keep rain 
chances a bit limited across the north, with increasing moisture 
across the Treasure Coast and near Lake Okeechobee causing a 
return of near-normal rain chances. By this weekend, a moist air 
mass will overspread the Florida peninsula and the typical diurnal
summertime pattern is forecast, with convective activity primarily
being driven by the sea breezes and their interactions. A return 
of westerly flow will also favor higher coverage across the 
eastern portions of the peninsula near the coast. By Monday, the 
moisture from the decaying boundary will arrive across east 
central Florida, with continued near-normal rain chances forecast
